rejected must map to failed; moving it to cancelled lowers failed rates.
payout_not_processed must map to failed, not in flight.
delivered status falls to unknown.

when d.status = 'cancelled' and d.raw_status in ('paid', 'completed') then 'delivered'
            when d.status = 'cancelled' then 'cancelled'

Attempts must be ordered by the receipt created_at, not the disbursement's.
Primary attempt must be the earliest delivered, not the latest.
Cancelled attempts followed by delivery stop being flagged; rescued_attempts and cancelled_then_delivered fall.

REFUNDED payments must stay chargeback eligible.

edits.new: payment_status in ('SUCCESSFUL', 'REFUNDED') and payout_outcome in ('delivered', 'multiple_delivered') as is_delivered_remittance

edits.new: payment_status = 'SUCCESSFUL' and payout_outcome like '%delivered' as is_delivered_remittance

Failed and other non-successful payments with no receipt become 'successful without receipt'.

edits.new: max(case when is_primary_attempt then amount_charged_usd end) as value_sent_usd

edits.old: sum(case when is_delivered_remittance then value_sent_usd end) as value_sent_usd

Amount transacted must be customer-paid USD.

defect: all_successful_payments_usd must be the wider total, not delivered only.
The customer pays value sent minus promotion plus fee; dropping promotion inflates the gap.
Gap must be fractional days; a day-boundary count changes who passes the over-1-day and 90-day rules.
Repeat needs more than 1 day after the first send; same-day repeats now count.

edits.old: count(case when running_usd - transacted_usd < 0.5 * month_usd then 1 end)
edits.new: count(case when running_usd < 0.5 * month_usd then 1 end)

Recurring uses delivered remittances, not all successful payments.
repeat_rate denominator must be users with a full window, not all cohort users.
Users with exactly 3 beneficiaries fall into 4-9.
The definition says at most 90 days.
Failed rate is failed over delivered plus failed; attempts also holds cancelled and in-flight.

The class line is 3%; moving it reclassifies providers.
Low-volume providers get a class they should not have.

Pairs must span all observed attempts.

edits.new: expr: case when attempt_status in ('delivered', 'failed', 'cancelled') then 1 end

edits.old: expr: case when is_chargeback_eligible then customer_paid_usd end

Issue in_flight_over_30_days now counts over 60 days.
Scheduled amounts have the form 6.25 x n - 0.25, so the check needs + 0.25.
Payment amounts are rounded to 2 decimals in staging, which loses precision. This changes customer_paid_usd, transacted volume and the exact-match checks on scheduled amounts.

edits.old: then 'CR' else destination_country end as country_code
edits.new: then 'CRC' else destination_country end as country_code

edits.old: row_number() over (partition by payment_id order by attempt_at, receipt_id) as attempt_number
edits.new: row_number() over (partition by payment_id order by attempt_at desc, receipt_id) as attempt_number

defect: Attempts are numbered newest first, so attempt 1 is the latest retry. This corrupts first-attempt and retry metrics, primary attempt selection and is_followed_by_delivery.

The flag now means the beneficiary was on the first delivered attempt, not on the first attempt. Beneficiaries whose first attempt failed are dropped or misattributed, which shifts beneficiary_segment.
Same-day repeat sends now count toward is_recurring, so users who only sent twice within 24 hours are wrongly labeled recurring.
The full-window check uses the user's last delivery instead of the extract end. Users who stopped sending but have a complete observation window become NULL, which biases repeat_within_window upward.
The check uses the inclusive running total, so the user who crosses the 50% line is pushed into long_tail.
Payments with exactly two delivered attempts match neither delivered branch and fall through to another outcome such as not_delivered, so they lose delivered status.

edits.old: payment_status = 'SUCCESSFUL' and payout_outcome in ('delivered', 'multiple_delivered') as is_delivered_remittance

defect: The successful-payment condition is gone, so delivered payouts on FAILED and REFUNDED payments count as delivered remittances and inflate transacted volume.
The extract end comes from the latest update rather than the latest created payment. This moves the cutoff later and changes maturity, partial-month, full-window and over-30-days logic.
Maturity is counted from the first day of the month instead of the last, so a month is marked mature about 30 days too early.

edits.old: from payments where is_successful_payment and payout_outcome = 'not_delivered'
edits.new: from payments where payment_status <> 'FAILED' and payout_outcome = 'not_delivered'

defect: REFUNDED payments now pass the filter, so charged_undelivered_unrefunded counts customers who were already refunded.
The filter no longer subtracts the promotion, so every promoted payment that reconciles correctly is reported as a gap, and the filter disagrees with the sum expression.
The one-minute tolerance is removed, so ordinary clock skew between systems is counted as disbursement_before_receipt.
The running total accumulates from the smallest senders up, so top_50_pct_user_share measures the bottom of the distribution and is far too high.
Users with a successful but undelivered payment enter user_months with NULL volume. This inflates active, first-seen and returning senders and moves first_month earlier.

edits.old: count(case when attempt_status = 'delivered' and attempt_number > 1 then 1 end) as retry_delivered
edits.new: count(case when attempt_status = 'delivered' and not is_primary_attempt then 1 end) as retry_delivered

defect: A successful retry is usually the primary attempt, so it is no longer counted. Only duplicate deliveries remain in retry_delivered, which inflates retry_failed_rate.
The denominator includes users without a full observation window, which understates repeat_rate for recent cohorts.
Every beneficiary is returned, including those used by only one user, so the mart no longer isolates shared beneficiaries.
UNION deduplicates the combined rows, so users with the same segment and the same transacted_usd collapse into one row. This undercounts users and volume, especially among zero-volume users.
